items.title: Dan Barrett interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995
items.q: Mr. Owen brought a couple of 78s by Tommy Dorsey and his orchestra

ctx.x: whether we play music or not, that we’re continually surrounded by music and he said many of you have parents who will play the radio when you’re in the car and if you go shopping you hear music in the supermarket, and if you go to the dentist’s office they usually have music playing. And he said of course there’s background music for television shows. So he pointed out how big a part music plays in our everyday lives, and he said that he knew that some of us were probably thinking that we would like to try and…

board, you know, they weighed a ton. Well he brought out one of those, and he had a couple of old 78s, and for our younger viewers, this is kind of funny. I never felt as old as I did when a student came over to my house for a lesson, and this young man was in his early 20s, and I wanted to play — I’m digressing but I’ll get back — but I wanted to play him a record by Tommy Dorsey, and I went to my 78 collection and he said, “what are those? Is that a record?” And I said, “yes, it’s a 78.” And he said, “oh, far…
Well I think it’s marvelous how somebody answers your questions and shows you the possibilities. You know, talk to us about how jazz improvisation shows us the innerds of the music.
